title: Keeping Up with Science: Coffee Drinkers: Fat, Muscle, and Hormones

elements.content: Welcome to Keeping Up with Science. Review the research context and metadata below:

Session Overview:
• Duration: 60 minutes
• Languages: 🇬🇧 English
• Level: Advanced (C1)
• Format: Interactive Discussion
Welcome! Share your initial thoughts on this topic. What personal experiences or observations come to mind right away?
Master the core scientific vocabulary and collocations for this topic (10 items):

• Metabolism ≠ Stagnation: the chemical processes that occur within a living organism to maintain life.
   Example: "Caffeine temporarily accelerates basal metabolism."

• Cortisol ≠ Serotonin: a steroid hormone regulating stress responses and metabolism.
   Example: "Drinking coffee on an empty stomach can elevate cortisol levels."

• Polyphenol ≠ Pro-oxidant: an antioxidant compound found abundantly in plant foods.
   Example: "Coffee is a major dietary source of protective polyphenols."

• Insulin Sensitivity ≠ Insulin resistance: how responsive cells are to insulin.
   Example: "Improved insulin sensitivity aids glucose uptake in muscle tissue."

• Lipid ≠ Carbohydrate: a class of organic compounds that are fatty acids or insoluble in water.
   Example: "Coffee compounds stimulate lipid oxidation during exercise."

• Bioactive ≠ Inert: having a biological effect on living tissue.
   Example: "Bioactive polyphenols exhibit strong anti-inflammatory properties."

• Endocrine ≠ Exocrine: relating to glands that secrete hormones directly into the bloodstream.
   Example: "Caffeine interacts with the human endocrine system."

• Preservation ≠ Degradation: the maintenance of something in its original state or in good condition.
   Example: "Lean muscle preservation is crucial during weight loss."

• Modulation ≠ Disruption: the exertion of a modifying or controlling influence on something.
   Example: "Hormonal modulation influences appetite and energy levels."

• Homeostasis ≠ Imbalance: the tendency toward a relatively stable equilibrium between interdependent elements.
   Example: "The body continuously strives for metabolic homeostasis."

elements.content: Study the scientific discourse patterns and grammar structures:
Use advanced stance markers and subjunctive structures: "It is imperative that researchers account for baseline cortisol levels when evaluating caffeine efficacy."
Analyze the core scientific findings and discuss the personal prompts in pairs:

• How does caffeine intake affect basal metabolism and lipid oxidation?

• Why do endocrinologists study the relationship between coffee consumption and cortisol spikes?

• What role do bioactive polyphenols play in improving insulin sensitivity?

• How does coffee consumption support lean muscle mass preservation during caloric deficit?

• In what ways does endocrine modulation affect daily metabolic homeostasis?
